scoreRule: 1 point per correct MC item; 10 points maximum; local provisional grade only
description: Ten newly written comprehension, interpretation and situational transfer questions; pending independent teacher review.

questions.q: Why does Leo ask the group who can come?
choices: He wants to arrange a picnic with his friends.
He is collecting money for a new school.
He needs somebody to teach Max to swim.
He wants to cancel a music performance.
questions.explanation: Leo proposes a picnic and checks who is available before arranging details.

questions.q: What does Ana's message tell us about the morning?
choices: She cannot visit the park at any time.
She is busy until her piano lesson finishes.
She has already spent the morning in the park.
She needs a bus to reach the café.
questions.explanation: Ana explains why noon suits her better than the morning.

questions.q: Why is it useful for Sam to name the café?
choices: The group must buy a full lunch there.
It is where Ana has her piano lesson.
It gives everyone one place that is easy to find.
The park has no other place to sit.
questions.explanation: Sam worries that the park is large and suggests a recognizable meeting point.

questions.q: Which two details make the final arrangement clear?
choices: The kind of fruit and Sam's music.
The number of sandwiches and the bus fare.
The exact piano piece Ana will play.
The meeting time and the café's green door.
questions.explanation: Leo confirms both noon and the clearly described café location.

questions.q: Why is Ana able to walk to the picnic?
choices: The bus does not run on Saturday.
Her home is close to Riverside Park.
She has forgotten her bus ticket.
She plans to meet Sam at his house.
questions.explanation: Ana says she lives near the park and can go there on foot.

questions.q: Why does Sam mention the big green door?
choices: He wants to paint the café.
He is asking the group to buy a green jacket.
He wants to describe the café's menu.
It helps his friends recognize the right café.
questions.explanation: The door is a visible landmark that makes the meeting easier.

questions.q: Why should the group begin the picnic on time?
choices: Leo's mother can stay only until three.
Ana must leave for her piano lesson at noon.
The park closes exactly at midday.
Sam's bus takes three hours to arrive.
questions.explanation: The limited time Leo's mother can stay makes punctuality important.

questions.q: A classmate is worried about finding friends in a large park. What can help?
choices: Tell everybody to enter from a different gate.
Leave the meeting place undecided.
Choose a clear landmark everyone can find.
Ask people not to bring phones.
questions.explanation: Sam uses the café near the lake as a recognizable point in a large park.

questions.q: What should a friend bring if the picnic is by the water?
choices: A thick coat because snow is expected.
A jacket for the wind, even on a sunny day.
A swimming ticket for the café.
A piano because Ana has a lesson.
questions.explanation: Leo warns that the lakeside can be windy despite sunshine.

questions.q: One friend can come only after eleven. Which plan follows the chat's example?
choices: Start the picnic before that friend's lesson ends.
Cancel the whole weekend immediately.
Tell the friend to skip the lesson.
Pick a time when that friend is free.
questions.explanation: The group agrees on noon so that Ana can finish her morning lesson.
